raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
# Description

`mxfp8_scaling_compute_partial_amax` and `mxfp8_scaling_partial_cast` launched one block per 32×128 tile of the whole rows x cols weight, even though each call handles only a 1D shard of it, and every thread then skipped the elements outside the shard. They now launch only the row tiles that hold the shard. With 64-way sharding this is 3-23x faster for the amax kernel and 2.3-20x for the cast kernel; the largest weights gain the most.

Fixes # (issue)

## Type of change

- [ ] Documentation change (change only to the documentation, either a fix or a new content)
- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Infra/Build change
- [ ] Code refactoring

## Changes

Please list the changes introduced in this PR:

- **`partial_row_tiles(rows, cols, start_offset, len)`** returns the first and past-the-end rows of the 32-row tiles that contain elements `[start_offset, start_offset + len)`, or an empty range when `len == 0`. Both launchers already require `rows % 32 == 0`, so the clamp to `rows` always lands on a tile boundary.
- **Both kernels take a `row_offset`**, and the tile row is `row_offset / 32 + blockIdx.y` in place of `blockIdx.y`. The per-element shard guard is unchanged, so partial first and last tiles behave exactly as before.
- **The grid's y dimension** covers only `[row_begin, row_end)`. An empty shard launches nothing.
- **The amax kernel's output contract is unchanged.** The full-grid kernel wrote amax 0 for every tile outside the shard. The launcher now writes those zeros with `cudaMemset2DAsync`, over exactly the columns the old kernel wrote: `blocks_x * 4` rowwise and `blocks_x * 128` columnwise, for the rows before `row_begin` and from `row_end` on. Callers that do not zero-initialise the amax buffers therefore see identical results. Padding rows beyond `rows` are not touched, as before.
- **The cast kernel** writes only elements inside the shard, so no fill is needed.
- **`NVTE_CHECK_CUDA(cudaGetLastError())`** is added after both launches.

# Checklist:

- [x] I have read and followed the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TransformerEngine/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.rst)
- [x] The functionality is complete
- [x] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
- [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [x] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes

Confidence Score: 5/5

**[Medium impact]** The PR appears safe to merge; no actionable issues were found.

Summary

Both partial MXFP8 kernels now launch only the row tiles that overlap the shard. - MXFP8 partial kernels launch only the row tiles touched by a shard. Reviews (3) · Last reviewed commit: ["Merge branch 'main' into mxfp8-partial-k..."](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/dd4afc1fae2149559e59ad9482c4b1acb438e7bc) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)
Hi @ksivaman - could you PTAL when you get a chance. Also want to get CI started on this. Thanks!

**Neighboring writes escape this test** The test promises to check that cast outputs outside the shard stay untouched, but `out_row` and `out_col` contain only the shard. Their sentinel values are all overwritten, so the checks cannot catch writes before or after the output slice. Real callers pass views into larger weight buffers. Allocate larger sentinel-filled buffers, pass shard views to the cast, and check both surrounding regions afterward. Include the empty shard with a nonempty backing buffer.

+@pytest.mark.skipif(not mxfp8_available, reason=reason_for_no_mxfp8)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("with_columnwise", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "h,w,bounds",
+    [
+        # Shard boundaries inside a row, on a row, and on a 32-row tile.
+        (256, 384, [0, 5, 384 * 31 + 7, 384 * 64, 384 * 64 + 1, 384 * 200 + 100, 256 * 384]),
+        # Shards inside one row tile, an empty shard, and one shard across many tiles.
+        (128, 2048, [0, 0, 100, 2048 * 32, 2048 * 33 - 1, 128 * 2048]),
+        # Columns that do not fill a 128-column tile.
+        (64, 96, [0, 1000, 64 * 96]),
+    ],
+)
+def test_mxfp8_partial_kernels_sharded(h, w, bounds, with_columnwise):
+    """Each rank's shard writes the amaxes of every matrix row, zero outside the shard, and
+    leaves the padding and the output outside the shard untouched."""
+    torch.cuda.manual_seed(1234)
+    full = torch.randn(h * w, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device="cuda")
+    blocks_x = (w + 127) // 128
+    sentinel = 7.0
+
+    def _pad(x, padding):
+        return (x + padding - 1) // padding * padding
+
+    row_shape = [_pad(h, 128), _pad(w // 32, 4)]
+    col_shape = [_pad(h // 32, 4), _pad(w, 128)]
+    scales = torch.randint(110, 135, row_shape, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    col_scales = torch.randint(110, 135, col_shape, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+    for start, end in zip(bounds[:-1], bounds[1:]):
+        inp = full[start:end]
+        row = torch.full(row_shape, sentinel, dtype=inp.dtype, device="cuda")
+        col = torch.full(col_shape, sentinel, dtype=inp.dtype, device="cuda")
+        omitted = col.flatten()[:0].view(0, 0)
+        tex.mxfp8_scaling_compute_partial_amax(
+            inp, row, col if with_columnwise else omitted, h, w, start
+        )
+
+        row_ref = torch.full_like(row, sentinel)
+        col_ref = torch.full_like(col, sentinel)
+        row_ref[:h, : blocks_x * 4] = 0
+        col_ref[: h // 32, : blocks_x * 128] = 0
+        compute_partial_amax_reference(inp, row_ref, col_ref, h, w, start)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(row, row_ref, atol=0, rtol=0)
+        if with_columnwise:
+            torch.testing.assert_close(col, col_ref, atol=0, rtol=0)
+        else:
+            assert (col == sentinel).all()
+
+        out_row = torch.full((end - start,), 0x5A, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
+        out_col = torch.full_like(out_row, 0x5A)
